foodName: Cucumber and yogurt salad (Kheere aur dahi ka salad)
dishTitle: Cucumber and Yogurt Salad (Kheere aur Dahi ka Salad)
instructions: Wash the cucumber thoroughly.
Peel it if required and cut it into small pieces.
Take plain yogurt in a mixing bowl and whisk until smooth.
Add cucumber pieces to the yogurt.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and lemon juice.
Mix all ingredients properly.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve fresh.
Place eggs in boiling water for 9-10 minutes. Cool in iced water, peel, and slice into halves.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add chopped onion and slit green chilli; sauté over medium heat for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, and salt; cook for 3 minutes until tomato breaks down.
Pour 1.5 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil.
Stir in the rolled oats, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 4 minutes until thick and creamy.
Transfer savory oats to a bowl, top with sliced boiled eggs, and serve warm.
Spoon chilled Greek yogurt into a clean breakfast bowl.
Rinse fresh berries under cold water and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Slice larger strawberries into quarters.
Arrange berries over the yogurt surface.
Scatter chia seeds and dust with a gentle pinch of cinnamon.
Serve immediately or chill for 10 minutes before enjoying.
Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve to remove natural saponin.
Add quinoa to a pot with 1 cup of water and a pinch of salt; simmer covered for 12-14 minutes until water is absorbed.
Heat 1 teaspoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add paneer cubes and sear for 2-3 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Wash baby spinach, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes.
In a wide meal bowl, layer the warm fluffy quinoa.
Arrange seared paneer, fresh spinach leaves, cucumber, and tomatoes side by side.
Drizzle fresh lemon juice and season with cracked black pepper and salt.

dishTitle: Spiced Roasted Makhana with Fragrant Chai
instructions: Heat ghee in a wide heavy kadai over low flame.
Add makhana and dry-roast continuously for 6-8 minutes until crisp and brittle to the touch.
Dust roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and black salt over the warm makhana; toss well to coat.
In a saucepan, bring water, crushed cardamom, and tea leaves to a boil for 2 minutes.
Add milk and simmer for 2 minutes until rich and aromatic.
Strain tea into a cup and serve warm alongside the crunchy spiced makhana.

dishTitle: Homestyle Dal, Phulka Roti & Seasonal Greens

ingredients.name: Yellow moong dal or toor dal

instructions: Rinse dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and half teaspoon salt for 3 whistles.
Knead whole wheat flour with water into a supple dough, divide into 2 balls, roll thin, and roast on a hot tawa until puffed.
Wash and finely chop the seasonal greens.
Heat ½ teaspoon oil in a pan, add minced garlic, and sauté chopped greens with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes.
In a small tadka pan, heat ½ teaspoon ghee, splutter cumin seeds, and fry chopped onion and tomato until soft.
Pour tadka into the cooked dal, mix well, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve warm tempered dal with fresh hot phulkas and garlic-sautéed greens.
In a small bowl, mix grated cheese, minced green chillies, diced capsicum, and black pepper.
Spread the cheesy chilli mixture evenly over one slice of bread.
Cover with the second slice and lightly press down.
Smear half teaspoon butter on the outside bread surface.
Toast on a medium-hot tawa or sandwich toaster for 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and golden and cheese melts.
Cut diagonally and serve hot.
Trim bread crusts if desired, or keep intact for added fiber.
Spread fresh mint-coriander chutney evenly on one side of each bread slice.
Wash, peel, and thinly slice the fresh cucumber.
Layer cucumber rounds closely over the bottom bread slice.
Sprinkle roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and a dash of black salt.
Close with the top bread slice, press gently, and slice diagonally into triangles.
Serve fresh and crisp.

foodName: Cheese and pineapple sandwich (Cheese aur ananas ka sandwich)
instructions: Pat the pineapple pieces completely dry using a kitchen towel to prevent soggy bread.
Combine grated cheese, chopped pineapple, and cracked black pepper in a small bowl.
Distribute the mixture evenly across one bread slice.
Top with the other slice and lightly butter the outer sides.
Toast on a medium pan or grill press for 2 minutes per side until golden brown and cheese is melted.
Slice in half and serve warm.

foodName: Cheese and tomato sandwich (Cheese aur tamatar ke sandwich)
instructions: Spread green chutney or herb spread evenly over both bread slices.
Place cheese over the base slice.
Arrange thin tomato slices neatly over the cheese.
Season lightly with black pepper, oregano, and salt.
Cover with the second slice, press gently, and slice into halves.
Enjoy fresh.

foodName: Peanut and tomato sandwich (Moongfali aur tamatar ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Peanut and Tomato Sandwich (Moongfali aur Tamatar ka Sandwich)

ingredients.name: Freshly ground black pepper & sea salt

instructions: Lightly toast bread slices if desired for a crisp texture.
Spread unsweetened peanut butter evenly across one bread slice.
Arrange fresh ripe tomato slices on top of the peanut butter layer.
Sprinkle cracked black pepper, a touch of sea salt, and fresh herbs.
Cap with the remaining bread slice and slice neatly in half.
Serve immediately.

foodName: Carrot apple sandwich (Gajar aur seb ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Carrot Apple Sandwich (Gajar aur Seb ka Sandwich)
instructions: Grate carrot and apple into a glass bowl.
Toss immediately with lemon juice to keep apple fresh and prevent browning.
Add shredded mint leaves, cracked black pepper, and black salt; mix well.
Pile the crunchy carrot-apple slaw generously onto a bread slice.
Cover with the second slice, press softly, and cut in half.
Serve as a revitalizing vegan lunch or snack.

foodName: Pea potato sandwich (toasted) (Matar aloo ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Toasted Pea and Potato Sandwich (Matar Aloo ka Sandwich)
instructions: In a bowl, mix mashed boiled potato, crushed green peas, spices, salt, and fresh coriander.
Spread the spiced vegetable filling evenly between two bread slices.
Brush a few drops of oil on the outside of the bread.
Toast on a hot skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden and crunchy.
Slice into triangles and serve with homemade mint chutney.

foodName: Pea keema sandwich (toasted) (Matar aur keema ka sandwich)

ingredients.name: Coarsely minced green peas & soya granules

instructions: Heat oil in a pan, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until aromatic.
Add crushed peas and soaked minced soya keema with spices and salt.
Cook for 4-5 minutes until dry and well combined, then cool slightly.
Place savory plant keema between bread slices.
Grill or pan-toast with minimal oil until deeply crisp.
Serve warm.
Mix mashed potato or crumbled silken tofu with salt and chili flakes.
Spread a thin layer over one side of the bread slices to act as a binder.
Press sesame seeds firmly into the layer so the surface is thoroughly covered.
Heat oil in a flat pan and place toast seed-side down over medium flame.
Cook for 3 minutes until sesame seeds turn fragrant and golden, flip and toast reverse side for 2 minutes.
Serve hot and crunchy.
Dry roast cracked wheat in a pressure cooker or saucepan for 3-4 minutes until nutty and light brown.
Pour in water, close the lid, and pressure cook on medium flame for 3 whistles (or simmer 15 mins in pot).
Release steam naturally and open the cooker.
Stir in jaggery powder and fragrant cardamom powder over low flame until melted.
Garnish with slivered almonds and serve warm.
In a dry saucepan, gently roast suji on low heat for 3 minutes until aromatic.
Slowly pour water or oat milk while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook over low flame for 4-5 minutes until smooth and gently thickened.
Fold in jaggery and cardamom powder, stirring until uniformly sweet.
Top with crushed walnuts and enjoy hot.
Combine rolled oats and water or soy milk in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then turn down heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring frequently until creamy.
Remove from heat, pour into a breakfast bowl, and arrange fresh banana slices on top.
Sprinkle cinnamon and ground flaxseed for omega-3 richness.

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds & turmeric
ingredients.quantity: ½ tsp mustard, ¼ tsp turmeric

instructions: Rinse rice flakes in a colander under running water for 30 seconds; drain completely and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves, green chilli, and diced onion.
Sauté until onion turns soft and translucent, then add turmeric powder and salt.
Stir in the softened poha and roasted peanuts gently so flakes do not break.
Cover with a lid and let steam on lowest heat for 2 minutes.
Finish with fresh lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves.
Heat half teaspoon oil in a large kadai over low flame.
Add curry leaves, roasted gram, and turmeric powder, letting them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add puffed rice and toss continuously for 3-4 minutes until extra crisp.
Season with rock salt and chaat masala.
Cool slightly and serve as a light, crunchy tea-time snack.
In a mixing bowl, combine besan, ajwain, turmeric, and salt.
Gradually whisk in water to make a smooth, pourable batter without lumps.
Fold in grated carrot, chopped spinach, and finely chopped onion.
Heat a non-stick tawa, brush lightly with oil, and pour a ladleful of batter, spreading into a round.
Cook on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until bubbles appear and underside is golden.
Flip and cook the other side for 2 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with mint or tomato dip.
Add fresh chilled curd, cold water, and raw sugar into a blender or traditional madhani pot.
Blend or churn vigorously for 45-60 seconds until a thick, velvety foam forms on top.
Add cardamom powder and rose water; give one final quick pulse.
Pour into a tall clay kulhad or glass, ensuring the rich froth sits on top.
Serve refreshingly cold.
Combine chilled curd, water, roasted cumin powder, and black salt in a blender.
Whisk or blend for 1 minute until smooth and frothy.
Pour into a chilled glass.
Garnish with crushed fresh mint leaves and a pinch of roasted cumin.
Serve as an invigorating digestive cooler.
Gently place eggs into a small saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch.
Bring water to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.
Once boiling, turn off heat, cover tightly with a lid, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Transfer eggs immediately to a bowl filled with iced water for 3 minutes to stop cooking.
Gently tap and peel shells under running water.
Slice eggs into halves, season with black pepper and rock salt, and serve.
Mash or slice the boiled egg in a bowl and mix with chopped onion, black pepper, and chaat masala.
Spread green chutney on both bread slices.
Layer the seasoned egg mixture generously over the bottom slice.
Top with second bread slice and lightly toast on a griddle with ½ teaspoon butter until golden crisp.
Cut in half and serve warm.

ingredients.name: Hung curd or light yogurt spread

instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted simmering water for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
Shred the chicken using two forks and let it cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix shredded chicken with hung curd, black pepper, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt.
Place crisp lettuce leaf and sliced cucumber on one bread slice.
Spoon creamy chicken spread evenly over the greens.
Cover with second slice, slice diagonally, and enjoy.
Spread mint-coriander green chutney on inner sides of both bread slices.
Layer warm cooked chicken shreds and crunchy sliced peppers on bread.
Close sandwich and press gently.
Brush skillet with olive oil, place sandwich, and toast over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve warm with fresh tomato dip.
In a salad bowl, blend light mayonnaise with grated carrot, cucumber, and sweet corn.
Season with freshly ground black pepper and a touch of salt.
Spread the chilled vegetable mayonnaise mixture thickly between two slices of whole wheat bread.
Trim edges if preferred and cut diagonally into finger sandwiches.
Serve fresh and crisp.

foodName: Egg and tomato sandwich (Ande aur tamatar ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Egg and Tomato Sandwich (Ande aur Tamatar ka Sandwich)
instructions: Lightly toast multigrain bread slices.
Spread mustard or chutney across both slices.
Alternate layers of sliced boiled egg and juicy red tomato rounds.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper and sea salt.
Top with the second slice, slice across, and serve immediately.

dishTitle: Indian Style Scrambled Eggs (Ande ki Bhurji)
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly with a fork.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat; sauté chopped onion and green chilli until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, and chili powder; sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Lower the flame and pour in the beaten eggs.
Stir gently and continuously for 2-3 minutes as soft curds form; do not overcook.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves and serve warm with roti or toast.
Fill a deep pan with water, add vinegar, and bring to a gentle, steady simmer (not a rolling boil).
Crack one cold egg into a small ramekin or teacup.
Swirl the simmering water with a spoon to create a gentle whirlpool in the center.
Carefully drop the egg into the whirlpool eye; the swirling water wraps whites around the yolk.
Poach gently for 3-4 minutes until whites are firm and yolk remains softly liquid.
Lift with a slotted spoon, blot on paper towel, season with pepper and salt, and serve on toast.
Warm oil or butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Carefully crack eggs directly into the pan without breaking the yolks.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set and edges turn slightly golden.
Spoon a little warm oil over whites if needed to finish setting.
Slide onto a plate, dust with sea salt and cracked black pepper, and serve warm.
In a small skillet, sauté sliced mushrooms, onion, and spinach with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes; set aside.
Whisk eggs in a bowl with salt, black pepper, and oregano until slightly bubbly.
Heat oil in an 8-inch non-stick skillet over medium-low flame.
Pour beaten eggs into skillet and tilt pan so it spreads into an even round.
When eggs are almost set on top, spoon the warm mushroom-spinach filling onto one half.
Gently fold the other half over the filling into a neat semicircle.
Cook for 30 seconds more and slide onto a warm plate.
Season chicken cubes with olive oil, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Sear on a hot grill pan or skillet for 4-5 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Wash salad greens, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes in ice-cold water, then spin dry.
Assemble chilled greens in a large bowl and top with warm grilled chicken.
Drizzle lemon juice and freshly cracked black pepper.
Toss lightly and serve fresh.
In a soup pot, bring chicken broth, minced ginger, and sweet corn to a boil.
Add minced chicken and simmer for 5-6 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and slowly pour into the simmering soup, stirring until thickened.
Turn down flame and slowly drizzle the beaten egg white in a thin stream while gently stirring to create delicate silky ribbons.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle chopped spring onion greens, and serve hot.
Warm milk in a small saucepan over low heat until steam gently rises (do not boil).
In a bowl, whisk egg yolk with jaggery and vanilla until pale and creamy.
Gradually pour 3 tablespoons of warm milk into the yolk while whisking briskly to temper.
Pour tempered yolk mixture back into the saucepan with remaining milk.
Cook over lowest heat for 3-4 minutes while stirring constantly until mixture lightly coats a spoon.
Pour into a mug, dust freshly grated nutmeg and cinnamon on top, and enjoy warm or chilled.
Grate fresh cucumber and gently squeeze out excess water with your palms.
Whisk plain yogurt in a mixing bowl until silky smooth.
Fold the grated cucumber into the whipped yogurt.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and finely chopped mint leaves.
Mix thoroughly, chill in refrigerator for 10 minutes, and serve cold.

foodName: Tomato onion raita (Tamatar aur pyaaz ka raita)
dishTitle: Tomato Onion Raita (Tamatar aur Pyaaz ka Raita)
instructions: Whisk yogurt until creamy and lump-free.
Add finely diced onion, tomato, and minced green chilli.
Stir in roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve chilled alongside rice, pulao, or roti.
Optionally steam sprouted moong for 2 minutes or use fresh raw sprouts for maximum crunch.
In a wide mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong, diced cucumber, and tomato.
Add bright pomegranate arils and chopped fresh coriander.
Drizzle freshly squeezed lemon juice over the mixture.
Season with chaat masala and black salt, toss lightly, and serve.
In a large bowl, place cooked, drained, room-temperature pulses.
Add diced bell peppers, crunchy carrots, and fresh cucumber.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, roasted cumin, black pepper, and salt in a cup.
Pour dressing over pulses and vegetables; toss gently until evenly coated.
Serve as a protein-dense vegan meal or side.
Immerse green leaves in ice-cold water for 5 minutes, then dry thoroughly in a spinner.
Tear greens into bite-sized pieces and arrange in a wide salad bowl.
Scatter sliced cucumber, radish rounds, and julienned carrots.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil and fresh lemon juice over the top.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper and rock salt, toss lightly, and serve at once.
Rinse dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles.
Heat ghee or oil in a pan, crackle cumin and mustard seeds.
Add chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, sautéing until fragrant and light golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and ground spices; cook until oil separates and tomatoes turn mushy.
Pour cooked dal into the tempering pan, add a little water if too thick, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and serve warm.
Wash moong dal until water runs clear.
Simmer dal in a pot with water, turmeric, grated ginger, and salt for 15 minutes until soft.
In a small pan, heat 1 teaspoon oil and splutter cumin seeds.
Add chopped tomato and cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour the fragrant tomato cumin tadka directly into the simmering moong dal.
Simmer together for 2 minutes, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve.
Blanch washed spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water to retain vibrant green color.
Blend blanched spinach with green chilli into a smooth puree.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds, minced garlic, ginger, and onion; sauté until translucent.
Add tomato puree, salt, and spices; cook until oil releases.
Pour in bright green spinach puree and simmer gently for 3-4 minutes.
Gently fold in fresh paneer cubes and warm through for 2 minutes.
Serve warm with phulkas or brown rice.
Rinse rice and moong dal together until water runs clear; soak for 15 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, splutter cumin seeds and black peppercorns.
Add grated ginger and turmeric powder, sautéing for 20 seconds.
Add drained rice and dal, stirring for 1 minute to coat with ghee and spices.
Pour in 3 cups of water and salt; close cooker lid.
Cook for 4 whistles on medium heat, then allow steam to subside naturally.
Open and stir lightly into a creamy comforting consistency; serve warm with curd.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot, add whole spices until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown.
Toss in mixed diced vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add drained basmati rice and gently stir for 1 minute without breaking grains.
Pour 1 cup hot water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Cover tightly, turn heat to lowest setting, and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes off heat, fluff gently with a fork, and serve.

ingredients.name: Turmeric, coriander, cumin & red chili powder
Garam masala & fresh coriander
ingredients.quantity: ¼ tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp coriander

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot, add whole cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté over medium heat until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until raw aroma dissipates.
Add pureed tomato and ground spices; cook until oil begins to separate from the masala.
Add chicken pieces and sear in the masala for 4-5 minutes until sealed.
Pour in ½ cup warm water, cover with lid, and simmer over low heat for 12-14 minutes until chicken is tender and juicy.
Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander, stir, and serve with rotis or steamed rice.

cookingTips: Rinse thick poha gently in a colander and let it rest for 5 minutes so the grains stay fluffy and never turn mushy.
instructions: Wash the thick poha gently in a strainer under running water and drain excess water completely.
Heat oil in a kadai or wide pan over medium heat and add mustard seeds; allow them to splutter.
Add curry leaves and slit green chilli, then sauté chopped onion for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add finely diced carrot and green peas; sauté for 4 minutes until tender.
Stir in turmeric powder and salt, then add the drained poha and mix gently without breaking the flakes.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2–3 minutes until heated through.
Turn off heat, drizzle lemon juice, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve warm.

cookingTips: Add a sprinkle of water while steaming on low flame if poha feels dry.
instructions: Rinse poha in a sieve and set aside for 5 minutes to soften evenly.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and chopped onion; sauté until soft.
Add turmeric powder, salt, and drained poha; toss gently to coat.
Cover and steam on low heat for 2 minutes.
Fold in roasted peanuts, lemon juice, and fresh coriander before serving.

cookingTips: Use room-temperature or lightly chilled fresh curd for a smooth, soothing texture.
instructions: Rinse poha twice in clean water and soak in a little water for 3 minutes until soft, then drain.
Whisk fresh curd in a bowl until creamy and lump-free.
Fold the softened poha into the whisked curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt, garnish with coriander, and serve fresh.
swaps: Cucumber and yogurt salad (Kheere aur dahi ka salad)

cookingTips: Steam or lightly sauté moong sprouts for 3 minutes before adding poha for easier digestion.
instructions: Rinse poha in a strainer and drain well.
Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, and sauté onion and green chilli for 2 minutes.
Add sprouted moong beans, turmeric, and salt; sauté for 3–4 minutes until tender.
Add drained poha, mix gently, and steam covered on low heat for 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

cookingTips: Dry roast semolina on low flame until aromatic without browning to prevent lumps when adding hot water.
instructions: Dry roast semolina in a pan over low heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant; transfer to a plate.
Heat oil in the same pan; add mustard seeds and urad dal until golden and crackling.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and onion; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add carrot and green peas and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour hot water and salt; bring to a gentle boil.
Slowly pour in roasted semolina while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 3 minutes until fluffy; serve warm.

cookingTips: Use a 1:2.5 ratio of roasted suji to boiling water for soft, non-sticky upma.
instructions: Dry roast semolina on low flame for 4 minutes until aromatic and set aside.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, and sauté curry leaves, green chilli, ginger, and onion for 2 minutes.
Add hot water and salt and bring to a boil.
Add roasted semolina gradually while stirring continuously.
Cover and cook on low flame for 2–3 minutes until water is absorbed; fluff and serve.

cookingTips: Toast bread cubes lightly before tossing in masala so they stay crisp outside and soft inside.
instructions: Cut bread slices into bite-sized cubes and lightly toast on a dry tawa for 2 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, and add curry leaves.
Sauté chopped onion for 2 minutes, then add tomato, turmeric, and salt; cook until soft.
Add bread cubes and toss well for 2–3 minutes so the masala coats evenly.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

cookingTips: Simmer sprouts in the spiced water for 3 minutes before adding suji so they cook through.
instructions: Dry roast semolina for 3–4 minutes on low heat and set aside.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, and sauté onion and green chilli.
Add sprouts, water, and salt; simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in roasted semolina gradually, cover, and cook on low heat for 3 minutes.

cookingTips: Do not over-boil vermicelli; drain or steam until just tender so strands remain separate.
instructions: Dry roast vermicelli in a pan for 3 minutes until light golden; transfer out.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves, onion, carrot, and peas; sauté for 3 minutes.
Add hot water and salt and bring to a boil.
Add roasted vermicelli, stir gently, cover and cook on low heat for 4–5 minutes until absorbed.

cookingTips: Grease idli moulds lightly and let idlis rest 2 minutes after steaming before unmoulding cleanly.
instructions: Stir the fermented idli batter gently without deflating the air pockets; check salt.
Lightly grease idli moulds and pour batter three-quarters full into each cavity.
Bring water to a boil in an idli steamer and place the stand inside.
Steam covered on medium-high heat for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Rest for 2 minutes, unmould with a wet spoon, and serve warm with sambar or chutney.

cookingTips: Rest the roasted rava batter for 10 minutes so the semolina absorbs liquid before steaming.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves, then roast semolina for 3 minutes.
Cool slightly, mix with water/plant curd, grated carrot, and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Stir in fruit salt gently just before steaming and spoon into greased idli moulds.
Steam covered for 10–12 minutes until fluffy and cooked through.

cookingTips: Spread batter on a medium-hot tawa starting from the center outward in smooth spirals.
instructions: Whisk dosa batter to a smooth pouring consistency.
Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa over medium heat and lightly brush with oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter in the center and spread outward in thin circular motions.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges and cook until golden crisp underneath.
Fold neatly and serve hot with sambar or chutney.

cookingTips: Keep the potato masala slightly moist so it spreads easily inside the crisp dosa.
instructions: Heat 1 tsp oil, crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves and sliced onion; sauté 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, salt, and mashed potato with 2 tbsp water; simmer 3 minutes to make potato masala.
Heat a tawa, spread a ladleful of dosa batter into a thin disc, and drizzle remaining oil.
Cook until crisp and golden, place potato masala in the center, fold, and serve hot.

cookingTips: Soak whole green moong for 4–6 hours and grind with ginger and green chilli for instant batter.
instructions: Grind soaked green moong with ginger, green chilli, cumin seeds, salt, and water into a smooth batter.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter, and spread thinly in circles.
Scatter chopped onion on top, drizzle oil around edges, and cook until crisp.
Fold and serve warm with ginger or tomato chutney.
swaps: Moong dal stuffed cheela/chilla (Moong dal ka cheela/chilla)

cookingTips: Press chopped toppings gently with a spatula so they stick to the batter when flipped.
instructions: Heat a tawa and pour a ladleful of thick batter without spreading too thin.
Immediately top with chopped onion, tomato, green chilli, and coriander.
Press toppings lightly, drizzle oil around edges, and cover for 2 minutes.
Flip and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes until golden; serve warm.

cookingTips: Rest besan batter for 10 minutes before cooking for soft, pliable chillas.
instructions: Whisk besan, turmeric, ajwain, salt, and water into a smooth lump-free batter.
Fold in chopped onion, tomato, and fresh coriander.
Heat a greased tawa, pour half the batter, and spread into a thin circle.
Cook on medium heat for 2 minutes per side until lightly browned; repeat and serve hot.
swaps: Gram flour and semolina chilla/cheela/savory pancake (Besan suji chilla/cheela)
Moong dal stuffed cheela/chilla (Moong dal ka cheela/chilla)

foodName: Gram flour and semolina chilla/cheela/savory pancake (Besan suji chilla/cheela)
cookingTips: Adding semolina gives crisp edges while gram flour keeps the center protein-rich.
instructions: Mix besan, semolina, spices, salt, and water; rest 10 minutes.
Stir in grated carrot and chopped spinach.
Spread onto a hot lightly greased tawa and cook 2–3 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

foodName: Moong dal stuffed cheela/chilla (Moong dal ka cheela/chilla)
cookingTips: Grind soaked yellow moong dal with ginger and minimal water for a smooth spreadable batter.
instructions: Blend soaked moong dal with ginger, green chilli, cumin, and water until smooth.
Heat a non-stick tawa and spread a ladleful of batter into a thin crepe.
Top with onion and tomato, drizzle oil, and cook 2 minutes per side until golden.

cookingTips: Season grated paneer stuffing just before filling so it stays crumbly and does not release water.
instructions: Whisk besan, turmeric, salt, and water into a smooth batter.
Toss crumbled paneer with chopped onion, coriander, cumin powder, and a pinch of salt.
Spread batter on a hot tawa, cook 2 minutes, flip, and cook 1 minute.
Place paneer stuffing in the center, fold over, and serve warm.

foodName: Tomato and cucumber sandwich (Tamatar aur kheere ka sandwich)
cookingTips: Pat sliced cucumber and tomato dry with a clean towel so the bread stays crisp.
instructions: Spread mint coriander chutney evenly on two whole wheat bread slices.
Layer thinly sliced cucumber and ripe tomato over one slice.
Sprinkle black pepper and chaat masala.
Cover with the second slice, cut diagonally, and serve fresh.

cookingTips: Use firm ripe tomatoes and grill on medium heat for crisp golden bread.
instructions: Layer sliced tomatoes on a bread slice and season with oregano, pepper, and salt.
Close the sandwich and brush the outer surfaces lightly with olive oil.
Grill in a sandwich maker or pan for 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
swaps: Tomato and cucumber sandwich (Tamatar aur kheere ka sandwich)

cookingTips: Roast broken wheat lightly before simmering for a nutty aroma.
instructions: Dry roast broken wheat in a saucepan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add water or almond milk and simmer for 12 minutes until grains are soft.
Stir in jaggery powder and cardamom powder until dissolved.
Top with chopped almonds and serve warm.

cookingTips: Keep simmer gentle after adding jaggery so plant milk does not split.
instructions: Dry roast vermicelli for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Add water or soy milk and cook for 7–8 minutes until tender.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder, simmer 1 minute, and serve warm.

foodName: Indian style egg bhujia (Anda bhujia (Indian style))
dishTitle: Anda Bhurji (Indian Style Spiced Scrambled Eggs)
cookingTips: Remove from heat while eggs are just set and moist; residual heat finishes cooking.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and sauté chopped onion and green chilli for 2 minutes.
Add tomato, turmeric, and salt; cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Crack eggs directly into the pan or pour beaten eggs in and stir gently on medium-low heat.
Scramble until soft curds form, garnish with coriander, and serve hot.

cookingTips: Sauté mushrooms first so excess moisture evaporates before adding cheese.

ingredients.name: Besan or eggless omelette batter / whole eggs

instructions: Sauté sliced mushrooms in a little oil for 3 minutes until golden and dry.
Pour whisked batter or eggs over the mushrooms on medium-low heat.
Sprinkle grated cheese, black pepper, and salt when nearly set.
Fold in half, cook 1 minute until cheese melts, and serve warm.

dishTitle: Cornflakes with Warm or Chilled Milk
cookingTips: Pour milk just before eating so cornflakes stay crunchy.
instructions: Place cornflakes in a breakfast bowl.
Pour toned milk over the cornflakes.
Top with fresh sliced fruit if desired and serve immediately.

cookingTips: Toss apples and bananas in fresh lemon juice right after cutting to prevent browning.
instructions: Wash, peel, and cube all fresh fruits into bite-sized pieces.
Place fruits in a chilled bowl and drizzle with fresh lemon juice.
Sprinkle chaat masala lightly, toss gently, and serve fresh.

cookingTips: Steam sprouts for 3 minutes if you prefer a softer texture.
instructions: Rinse sprouted green moong beans thoroughly and drain.
Combine sprouts, diced tomato, onion, and cucumber in a mixing bowl.
Add lemon juice, roasted cumin powder, black salt, and fresh coriander.
Toss well and serve immediately.

cookingTips: Toss spices with hot boiled corn kernels so flavors coat evenly.
instructions: Boil or steam sweet corn kernels for 5 minutes until plump and tender; drain well.
Transfer warm corn to a bowl and add chopped onion, tomato, chaat masala, and chilli powder.
Drizzle lemon juice, garnish with coriander, toss, and serve warm.

cookingTips: Simmer covered on low flame so apples soften in their natural juices.
instructions: Core, peel, and slice apples evenly.
Place apples, water, and cinnamon in a small saucepan.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 8–10 minutes until tender.
Finish with a splash of lemon juice and serve warm.

cookingTips: Soak rolled oats and chia seeds in water or plant milk for 10 minutes for a creamier blend.
instructions: Add chopped apple, rolled oats, chia seeds, cinnamon, and water/almond milk into a blender.
Blend on high speed for 45 seconds until completely smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass and serve immediately.

cookingTips: Use ripe red tomatoes for natural sweetness without added sugar.
instructions: Boil tomatoes and crushed garlic with water for 10 minutes until skins peel easily.
Blend briefly and strain through a fine mesh strainer to obtain a clear broth.
Return to heat, season with salt and crushed black pepper, and simmer 3 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

cookingTips: Do not over-boil spinach so the soup keeps its vibrant green color and nutrients.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté garlic and onion for 2 minutes.
Add washed spinach leaves and wilt for 2 minutes.
Pour in water, simmer 3 minutes, then blend smooth.
Return to pan, season with black pepper and salt, heat through, and serve.

cookingTips: Cut vegetables into small uniform dice so they cook evenly in 10 minutes.
instructions: Heat oil in a saucepan and sauté minced ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add diced vegetables and corn; toss for 2 minutes.
Pour water and simmer covered for 10 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with black pepper and salt and serve hot.

cookingTips: Blend half the corn into a creamy base and leave the other half whole for texture.
instructions: Coarsely blend half of the sweet corn with 3 tbsp water.
Bring water to a boil in a pan, add blended corn, whole corn, and diced vegetables; simmer 6 minutes.
Stir in dissolved cornstarch and simmer 2 minutes until lightly thickened.
Season with white pepper and salt and serve hot.

cookingTips: A squeeze of lemon at the end brightens the earthy flavor of lentils.
instructions: Heat oil, sauté onion, carrot, and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add rinsed lentils, cumin, turmeric, water, and salt; simmer 15 minutes until soft.
Blend partially or fully until creamy, finish with lemon juice, and serve warm.

cookingTips: Simmer pumpkin until fork-tender before pureeing for a velvety texture without cream.
instructions: Heat olive oil and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add cubed pumpkin, water, and salt; simmer covered for 12 minutes until soft.
Blend until silky smooth, season with black pepper, and serve warm.

foodName: Gram flour and semolina dhokla (Besan suji dhokla)
cookingTips: Steam immediately after whisking in fruit salt so the dhokla rises light and spongy.
instructions: Whisk besan, semolina, ginger-chilli paste, lemon juice, salt, and water into a smooth batter; rest 10 minutes.
Stir in fruit salt gently until frothy and pour into a greased steaming tin.
Steam covered for 12–15 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Prepare tempering with heated oil, mustard seeds, and curry leaves; spoon over cut dhokla squares and serve.

foodName: Carrot and spinach raita (Gajar aur palak ka raita)
cookingTips: Squeeze excess water from blanched spinach so the raita stays thick and creamy.
instructions: Blanch spinach leaves in hot water for 2 minutes, cool, squeeze dry, and finely chop.
Whisk fresh yogurt until smooth.
Fold in grated carrot, chopped spinach, roasted cumin powder, and black salt.
Serve chilled.
swaps: Tomato onion raita (Tamatar aur pyaaz ka raita)

cookingTips: Rest kneaded dough covered for 15 minutes so chapatis stay soft for hours.
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour with warm water and salt for 5 minutes into a smooth, pliable dough; rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 2 equal balls and roll each into a thin 6-inch circle using dry flour.
Place on a hot tawa; when small bubbles appear, flip and cook the second side.
Press gently with a clean folded cloth or puff directly over flame until soft spots appear; serve warm.

cookingTips: Fold rolled dough with a light brush of oil to create flaky layers.
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour, salt, and water into a soft dough; rest 10 minutes.
Roll into a disc, brush with oil, fold into a triangle, and roll again evenly.
Cook on a hot tawa for 2 minutes per side with a light brush of oil until golden brown.

cookingTips: Cool boiled potatoes completely before mashing so the stuffing stays dry and easy to roll.
instructions: Knead whole wheat flour with water and salt into a soft dough.
Mix mashed potato with green chilli, coriander, cumin powder, amchur, and salt.
Stuff spiced potato filling inside a dough ball, seal edges, and roll gently.
Roast on a hot tawa with a brush of oil for 2–3 minutes per side until crisp and golden.

cookingTips: Add salt to grated cauliflower just before stuffing to prevent moisture release.
instructions: Knead a soft whole wheat dough and rest 10 minutes.
Combine grated cauliflower, ginger, green chilli, ajwain, coriander powder, and salt.
Stuff mixture inside rolled dough, seal, and roll gently.
Cook on a hot tawa with oil until golden spots appear on both sides.

cookingTips: Grate fresh paneer finely so it rolls evenly without tearing the dough.
instructions: Prepare soft whole wheat dough and rest 10 minutes.
Mix grated paneer, onion, coriander, cumin, garam masala, and salt.
Fill dough ball with paneer stuffing, seal, and roll out gently.
Roast on a hot tawa with ghee/oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden.

cookingTips: Wash and chop only tender methi leaves to avoid bitterness.
instructions: Combine wheat flour, chopped methi leaves, turmeric, cumin, salt, and water into a firm dough.
Divide into 2 portions and roll out evenly.
Roast on a hot tawa brushing lightly with oil until cooked through.
swaps: Besan and spinach parantha/paratha (Besan aur palak ka parantha/paratha)

cookingTips: Rinse rice twice until water runs mostly clear and soak 15 minutes for fluffy separate grains.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly and soak for 15 minutes; drain.
Bring water to a boil in a saucepan, add rice, and stir once.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer 12 minutes until water is absorbed.
Let rest covered 5 minutes, fluff gently with a fork, and serve.

cookingTips: Add lemon juice off the heat so it stays bright and never turns bitter.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, and toast chana dal and peanuts until crisp.
Add curry leaves, green chilli, and turmeric powder.
Turn off heat, fold in cooked rice and salt gently.
Drizzle fresh lemon juice, toss evenly, and serve.
swaps: Curd rice (Dahi bhaat/Dahi chawal/ Perugu annam/Daddojanam/Thayir saadam)

foodName: Curd rice (Dahi bhaat/Dahi chawal/ Perugu annam/Daddojanam/Thayir saadam)
cookingTips: Mash warm cooked rice slightly before mixing curd so it absorbs smoothly.
instructions: Lightly mash warm cooked rice and allow it to cool to lukewarm.
Mix in whisked curd and salt until creamy.
Heat oil in a small tadka pan; crackle mustard seeds, urad dal, curry leaves, and ginger.
Pour tempering over the curd rice, mix well, and serve.

cookingTips: Soak basmati rice for 20 minutes and use a 1:2 rice-to-water ratio for long fluffy grains.
instructions: Heat oil in a pot, add whole spices, and sauté sliced onion and ginger-garlic paste for 3 minutes.
Add mixed vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes.
Stir in drained basmati rice gently for 1 minute.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low heat for 12–14 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

cookingTips: Cook rice to 80% doneness before layering with spiced vegetables for distinct biryani grains.
instructions: Boil soaked basmati rice with a pinch of salt until 80% cooked; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a heavy pot; sauté onions until golden, then add tomato, vegetables, biryani masala, and salt.
Cook covered for 6 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Layer par-cooked rice, mint, and coriander over the vegetable masala.
Seal tightly and steam on very low heat for 10 minutes; fluff gently and serve.

cookingTips: Use equal parts rice and split yellow moong dal for balanced protein and easy digestion.
instructions: Heat oil in a pressure cooker or pot; crackle cumin seeds and sauté grated ginger.
Add chopped vegetables, rice, moong dal, turmeric, salt, and water.
Pressure cook for 3 whistles (or simmer covered 18 minutes) until soft and creamy.
Adjust consistency with warm water if needed and serve hot.

cookingTips: Rinse quinoa thoroughly under running water to remove natural bitter saponins.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot and crackle cumin seeds.
Add rinsed quinoa, moong dal, carrot, peas, turmeric, salt, and water.
Simmer covered for 15–18 minutes until quinoa and dal are soft and creamy; serve warm.

cookingTips: Fold chopped spinach in during the last 4 minutes to preserve bright color.
instructions: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add rice, moong dal, turmeric, salt, and water; cook until nearly soft.
Stir in chopped spinach and simmer 4 minutes until wilted and blended; serve warm.
swaps: Arhar with spinach (Arhar dal aur palak)

cookingTips: Dry roast daliya for 2 minutes first so each grain cooks fluffy yet comforting.
instructions: Heat oil in a pressure cooker; crackle cumin seeds and sauté vegetables for 2 minutes.
Add daliya, moong dal, turmeric, salt, and water.
Cook for 3 whistles or simmer covered 18 minutes until soft and serve hot.

cookingTips: Simmer sambar gently for 5 minutes after adding tamarind and sambar powder so flavors meld.
instructions: Simmer chopped vegetables in tamarind water with salt and sambar powder for 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in mashed cooked toor dal and water; simmer 5 minutes.
Prepare tempering by crackling mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil.
Pour tempering over sambar, garnish with coriander, and serve hot.
swaps: Rasam with tamarind (Puli rasam/ Chintapandu rasam/ Charu/Saaru)

cookingTips: Plunge blanched spinach immediately into cold water to lock in bright green color.
instructions: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, transfer to cold water, and blend into a smooth puree.
Heat oil/ghee in a pan, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add tomato puree and cook 3 minutes until thickened.
Stir in spinach puree, garam masala, and salt; simmer 3 minutes.
Fold in paneer cubes, simmer 2 minutes, and serve warm.

cookingTips: Keep capsicum and onion cubes slightly crunchy for authentic kadhai texture.
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai; sauté chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste for 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree, crushed coriander seeds, chilli, and salt; cook 4 minutes.
Toss in capsicum and onion cubes; sauté 2 minutes.
Add paneer cubes, mix gently, cook 2 minutes, and serve hot.

cookingTips: Simmer paneer cubes gently at the end so they stay soft and soak up the gravy.
instructions: Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add tomato puree, spices, and salt; cook 4 minutes.
Add green peas and water; simmer 6 minutes until peas are tender.
Add paneer cubes, simmer 3 minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve.

cookingTips: Use low-fat milk or whisked yogurt with cashew paste for a rich yet balanced gravy.
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan; sauté onion puree and tomato puree for 5 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste, cardamom, garam masala, and salt; cook 2 minutes.
Lower heat, whisk in milk gradually, add paneer cubes, and simmer 3 minutes.

cookingTips: Pan-sear paneer cubes instead of deep frying to keep calories controlled.
instructions: Pan-sear paneer cubes in 1 tsp oil until lightly golden; set aside.
In the same pan, sauté garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, and bell pepper on high heat for 2 minutes.
Toss in soy sauce, vinegar, pepper, salt, and seared paneer for 1 minute; serve hot.

cookingTips: Soak chana dal for 30 minutes so the lentils cook tender while keeping their shape.
instructions: Pressure cook soaked chana dal with turmeric, salt, and water for 3–4 whistles until soft.
Heat oil in a pan, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté ginger-garlic, onion, and tomato until soft.
Pour cooked chana dal into the tadka, simmer 4 minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve.
swaps: Washed moong dal (Dhuli moong ki dal)

foodName: Washed moong dal (Dhuli moong ki dal)
cookingTips: Skim any surface foam while boiling moong dal for a clean, light broth.
instructions: Simmer rinsed moong dal with turmeric, salt, and water for 12–15 minutes until soft.
Heat oil in a small pan; sizzle cumin seeds and garlic, then cook chopped tomato for 2 minutes.
Pour tempering into the dal, simmer 2 minutes, and serve hot.

cookingTips: Whole masoor cooks quickly without lengthy soaking.
instructions: Boil or pressure cook rinsed masoor dal with water and salt for 15 minutes until tender.
Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté onion, ginger-garlic, and tomato with garam masala.
Combine with cooked dal, simmer 4 minutes, and serve.
swaps: Washed moong dal (Dhuli moong ki dal)

foodName: Arhar with spinach (Arhar dal aur palak)
cookingTips: Adding spinach to cooked toor dal preserves iron absorption and fresh flavor.
instructions: Cook toor dal with turmeric, salt, and water until soft.
Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, sauté garlic and tomato, then wilt chopped spinach for 2 minutes.
Pour cooked dal in, simmer together 4 minutes, and serve hot.
swaps: Washed moong dal (Dhuli moong ki dal)

cookingTips: Soak kidney beans overnight and mash a few cooked beans into the gravy for natural thickness.
instructions: Pressure cook soaked rajma with water and salt for 5–6 whistles until tender.
Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden brown.
Add tomato puree and spices; cook 4 minutes.
Add cooked rajma with its broth, mash a few beans, and simmer 8 minutes before serving.

cookingTips: Simmer slowly on low heat after mashing a portion of lentils for creamy body.
instructions: Pressure cook soaked urad dal and rajma with water and salt until completely soft.
Heat oil, sauté ginger-garlic paste and tomato puree with spices for 5 minutes.
Add cooked lentils, mash lightly, and simmer on low heat 12–15 minutes until rich and creamy.

cookingTips: Roast brinjal until skin chars and flesh is completely soft for authentic smoky flavor.
instructions: Roast whole brinjal over direct flame or oven until soft and charred; cool, peel, and mash pulp.
Heat oil, sauté garlic, green chilli, and onion for 3 minutes.
Add tomato, peas, and salt; cook 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in mashed brinjal, cook 5 minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve.

cookingTips: Wipe washed okra completely dry before slicing to prevent sliminess.
instructions: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté sliced onion for 2 minutes.
Add sliced okra and turmeric; cook uncovered on medium heat for 8 minutes stirring gently.
Add coriander powder, amchur, and salt; cook 2 more minutes and serve.

cookingTips: Cook covered on low heat without adding water so cauliflower stays firm and flavorful.
instructions: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté ginger for 30 seconds.
Add potato cubes, cauliflower florets, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt; toss well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12–14 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in chopped tomato for 2 minutes, garnish with coriander, and serve.

cookingTips: Simmer potatoes and peas together until potatoes lightly thicken the tomato gravy.
instructions: Heat oil, crackle cumin, and sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until soft.
Add tomato and spices; cook 3 minutes.
Add potato cubes, peas, water, and salt; cover and simmer 12 minutes until tender.

cookingTips: Cook potatoes 80% before adding chopped spinach so greens stay vibrant.
instructions: Heat oil, crackle cumin seeds, and sauté garlic for 30 seconds.
Add cubed potatoes, turmeric, and salt; cover and cook 8 minutes until almost tender.
Add chopped spinach and chilli powder; toss uncovered for 4–5 minutes until wilted and dry.

foodName: Beans with coconut (Nariyal aur sem/phali; Beans thoran)
cookingTips: Finish with fresh grated coconut off the heat to keep it sweet and tender.
instructions: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, and add curry leaves and green chilli.
Add chopped beans, turmeric, salt, and 2 tbsp water; cover and steam 6 minutes.
Fold in grated coconut, toss 1 minute, and serve warm.

cookingTips: Cook sliced mushrooms on medium-high briefly so they brown instead of steaming.
instructions: Heat oil, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until soft.
Add tomato and spices; cook 3 minutes.
Add mushrooms, green peas, and salt; cook 8 minutes until tender and serve.

cookingTips: Sear mushrooms first until moisture evaporates before wilting spinach.
instructions: Heat olive oil, sauté garlic and mushrooms for 5 minutes until browned.
Toss in spinach, black pepper, and salt; cook 2 minutes until wilted and serve.

cookingTips: Lightly sear turmeric-rubbed fish pieces before simmering so they stay intact in the mustard-tomato gravy.

ingredients.name: Rohu or firm white fish fillets

instructions: Rub fish fillets with a pinch of turmeric and salt; set aside 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a pan and sear fish 2 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, temper kalonji and green chilli, then sauté onion and tomato with cumin and turmeric.
Pour water and salt, bring to a simmer, gently slide seared fish in, and cook 6 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve warm with steamed rice.

cookingTips: Cook on low flame with a tight lid so chicken stays succulent in its own juices.
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot; sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add tomato puree and spices; cook 4 minutes.
Lower heat, stir in whisked yogurt and chicken pieces, and sear for 4 minutes.
Cover tightly and simmer on low heat 18–20 minutes until chicken is tender; garnish with coriander.

cookingTips: Add half the onions at the start for gravy body and crisp onion petals near the end for classic Do Pyaza sweetness.
instructions: Heat oil in a pressure cooker; sauté whole spices, chopped onion, and ginger-garlic paste until browned.
Add mutton, tomato, spices, and salt; sear 5 minutes.
Add water and pressure cook for 4–5 whistles until mutton is tender.
Stir in remaining onion petals and simmer uncovered 4 minutes until gravy thickens.

cookingTips: Marinate chicken in spiced yogurt for 20 minutes before pan-searing for tender bites.
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes with yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, and salt; pan-sear until cooked.
Heat butter in a pan, sauté remaining ginger-garlic paste and tomato puree 6 minutes.
Add garam masala, kasuri methi, and seared chicken; simmer 5 minutes and serve warm.

cookingTips: Make shallow slashes on chicken pieces so yogurt-spice marinade penetrates deeply.
instructions: Score chicken pieces and coat in lemon juice, salt, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and spices; rest 20 minutes.
Brush lightly with oil and roast in a preheated oven (200°C) or covered grill pan for 20–22 minutes, turning once.
Serve hot with onion rings and lemon wedges.

cookingTips: Whisk yogurt well and add on low heat to keep the korma sauce silky.
instructions: Sauté sliced onion in oil until crisp golden; crush finely.
Add chicken, ginger-garlic paste, spices, and salt; sear 5 minutes.
Stir in yogurt and crushed browned onions; cover and simmer 15 minutes until tender.

cookingTips: Sauté chicken briefly with whole spices before adding soaked rice for aromatic stock.
instructions: Heat oil, sauté whole spices, sliced onion, and ginger-garlic paste 3 minutes.
Add chicken and salt; cook 5 minutes until seared.
Add drained rice and water; cover and simmer 14 minutes until rice and chicken are cooked through.

cookingTips: Prick boiled eggs lightly with a fork before simmering so spices infuse evenly.
instructions: Prick boiled eggs gently and pan-sear with a pinch of turmeric for 2 minutes.
Sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste in oil until golden, then add tomato puree and spices.
Add water and salt, simmer 5 minutes, add eggs, and cook 3 more minutes.
swaps: Indian style egg bhujia (Anda bhujia (Indian style))

cookingTips: Avoid stirring vigorously once fish is in the curry; gently swirl the pan instead.
instructions: Heat oil and sauté ginger-garlic paste and onion-tomato puree with spices for 5 minutes.
Add water and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Slide fish pieces in carefully and simmer covered 7–8 minutes until flaky and cooked.

cookingTips: Pat fish dry before marinating so spices cling well during grilling.
instructions: Marinate fish cubes in lemon juice, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, ajwain, and salt for 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear with oil for 3–4 minutes per side until lightly charred and flaky.

cookingTips: Chill boiled eggs before wrapping in mashed potato-pea coating so the shell holds cleanly.
instructions: Season mashed potato and crushed peas with garam masala, black pepper, and salt.
Wrap the spiced potato mixture evenly around a peeled boiled egg.
Roll lightly in whole wheat breadcrumbs, brush with oil, and bake/air-fry at 190°C for 14 minutes until crisp.

cookingTips: Place pan-seared koftas into the warm gravy right before serving.
instructions: Coat boiled egg in seasoned potato-besan mix and pan-sear until golden.
Sauté ginger-garlic paste and onion-tomato puree with garam masala and salt for 5 minutes.
Add a splash of water to form a smooth gravy, halve the kofta, place in gravy, and serve warm.

dishTitle: Light Yogurt & Egg Quick Mayonnaise Dip
cookingTips: Use pasteurized egg or thick hung yogurt base and whisk steadily while drizzling oil.
instructions: Whisk egg yolk, mustard powder, vinegar, and salt in a clean bowl.
Drizzle olive oil drop by drop while whisking continuously until emulsified.
Fold in hung yogurt and black pepper until light and creamy; chill until ready to use.
